previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and chronic anticoagulation presented with a three-week history of epigastric pain, nausea, and melena. She was found to have acute on chronic gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to NSAID use and a supratherapeutic INR of 11.6 while on warfarin. She received five units of packed red blood cells and six units of fresh frozen plasma, with vitamin K administration to reverse coagulopathy. An EGD revealed esophagitis and gastritis without active bleeding, and a positive H. pylori antibody test was noted. Colonoscopy showed diverticulosis without active bleeding. Her heart failure worsened during admission with pulmonary edema, managed with IV and oral diuretics. She fell near discharge, resulting in wrist and knee pain; imaging showed no fractures, but she was prescribed a walker and wrist splint for safety. Warfarin was held during the bleed and restarted at discharge at a lower dose. She was discharged home with services on optimized heart failure and GI protective medications, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs and monitor for rebleeding.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with h/o GIB bleeding in ___ in the setting 
of NSAID and coumadin use who presents with acute blood loss 
anemia.  

* Anemia, Lower GI bleed - She was admitted with a Hct drop from 
39 to 24 in the setting of a slightly supratherapeutic INR.  Her 
coumadin was held on admission, but given that she was 
hemodynamically stable, she did not receive FFP or vitamin K.  
In the emergency room, she had a NG lavage that was negative.  
She was started on a IV PPI BID and transfused 2 units of PRBC.  
She was seen by the inpatient GI team and on further discussion 
with her son, ___, the HCP, he did not want her to have another 
colonoscopy.  In light of this, she transfused PRBC and her Hct 
were closely monitored.  She had guaiac positive bowel movements 
in the hospital, but her Hct remained stable.  

Regarding her chronic anticoagulation, her PMD was contacted to 
discuss whether coumadin should be continued.  Given her history 
of chronic PE/DVT, her PMD felt that she needed to be continued 
on anticoagulation at this point.  Her coumadin was held during 
her hospitalization given her supratherapeutic INR.  She will 
need to have her INR checked as described below.  On further 
discussion with GI, they would not pursue capsule study as an 
outpatient at this time.

* Hypoxia - On admission, her oxygen saturation was 88% on room 
air and corrected with oxygen.  Her CXR revealed mild pulmonary 
edema and she was restarted on her home lasix after a one time 
dose of 60 mg IV.  Her BNP was not elevated.  With diuresis, her 
oxygenation normalized.  

* Diastolic heart failure - Given evidence of pulmonary edema on 
CXR, a repeat TTE was obtained which showed worsening of MR and 
pulmonary hypertension.  She has an EF of 55%.  She was 
restarted on her lasix and metoprolol was continued.  

* Hypertension - Metoprolol was initially held and restarted 
during her hosptialization.  

* Atypical chest pain - She had 2 episodes of chest pain, but 
had no EKG changes and her troponins were negative x 3.  Aspirin 
was not given in the setting of her GI bleed.  She has chronic 
chest pain and had been started on tramadol as an outpatient.  
This was restarted in the hospital and helped with her pain.

* Headache - Worsened on admission, but repeat head imaging did 
not show new bleed or large ischemic event.  Her headache 
improved during her hospitalization without further 
intervention.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with hypoxia on presentation, please evaluate
for pneumonia or CHF.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH

There is unchanged cardiomegaly.  Also present is peribronchial thickening and
right fissural fluid concerning for early interstitial edema.  There is a new
small right pleural effusion. The mediastinal silhouette, hilar contours and
pleural surfaces are otherwise unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
CHF with mild interstitial edema and small right pleural effusion.

HISTORY:  Pleuritic chest pain and hypoxia, to evaluate for CHF and pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there are lower lung volumes. 
Continued enlargement of the cardiac silhouette with increasing engorgement of
ill-defined pulmonary vessels, consistent with pulmonary vascular congestion. 
Blunting of the right costophrenic angle is consistent with pleural effusion. 
Bibasilar atelectatic changes are seen.

IMPRESSION:  Developing pulmonary edema with right pleural effusion.
